newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Hellenic eyes Greece for expansion.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Hellenic eyes Greece for expansion.

text.p: Cyprus-based Hellenic Bank is firming up its plans for eventual expansion into the Greek market, the chairman of the Cypriot bank said on Wednesday.

"Our intention is to create a branch in a central area of Athens which will be an extension of the network of branches in Cyprus," bank chairman and general manager Panos Ghalanos told a news conference.
The bank, Cyprus's third largest, expects to offer its services in Greece to current Cypriot corporate clients who have also expanded their business there.
Ghalanos said the bank was currently studying some 10 proposed sites in the Greek capital to set up its new branch.
The bank has also expressed an interest in acquiring a majority stake in the Greek state-controlled Bank of Central Greece currently held by Agrotiki Bank.
Cypriot owned Hellenic bought the Cyprus onshore operations of Barclays Bank a year ago in a deal worth 8.5 million pounds ($16.7 million).

It reported preliminary pre-tax profits of 3.4 million pounds in 1996, compared with 4.75 million in 1995. Operating profit last year was up 38.7 percent, but the cost of the Barclays purchase and an early retirement scheme after the merger were included in the 1996 results.
In the same year its capital base increased by 56.7 percent to reach 62 million pounds. Deposits rose 91 percent to 841 million pounds and loans by 77.6 million to 533 million pounds.
The bank is now in the final stage of negotiations with an international investment company to branch out into offering mutual investment funds in Cyprus.

"It will cover all the investment needs of institutional and private investors," said George Trypatsas, manager of Hellenic Bank Investments. He declined to mention the name of their negotiating partners, but said that an announcement could be made in the next few days.
Hellenic Bank is due to hold its annual general meeting in Nicosia on Thursday.
